title: Tria capita ex opere quodam majori inedito de theoria lunae

deep.reconstruction:
Context: a chapter on the apparent diameters and true hourly motions of the Sun and Moon, for use in computing lunar eclipses. On this page Euler treats the Sun.

§1. U is the mean anomaly, V the eccentric anomaly and θ the true longitude/anomaly, with e = 0.0167595. Anomalies are counted from the apogee, as was usual in 18th-century solar tables. Hence Kepler's equation reads U = V + e sin V and the distance is y = a(1 + e cos V), with a = 100000.
- The apparent diameter scales as a/y, so diameter = 1933''/(1 + e cos V), taking 32'13'' at mean distance.
- Expanding 1/(1+x) with x = e cos V up to x³, and linearising powers of cosine (cos²V = (1+cos2V)/2, cos³V = (3cosV + cos3V)/4), gives 1933''(1 - e cosV + ½e² + ½e² cos2V - ¾e³ cosV - ¼e³ cos3V).
- The horizontal parallax scales the same way: 12.5''(1 + ½e² - (e + ¾e³)cosV + ½e² cos2V - ¼e³ cos3V).

§2. Numerically, ½e² ≈ 0.00014 and e + ¾e³ = 0.0167630.
- Diameter ≈ 1933'' - 32.4'' cos V + 0.27'' cos 2V. The last term is under half a second, so diameter = 32'13'' - 32.4 cos V and semidiameter = 16'6.5'' - 16.2 cos V. Euler gives the logarithms of the coefficients in parentheses.
- Parallax = 12.5'' - 0.2'' cos V. This lies between about 12'' at apogee and 13'' at perigee, so the correction can practically be ignored.

§3. True hourly motion.
- From dU = (1 + e cos V) dV and dθ = √(1-e²) dV/(1 + e cos V) one gets dθ/dU = √(1-e²)/(1 + e cos V)², i.e. the area law in the form dθ/dU = √(1-e²)(a/y)².
- Expanding (1+x)^-2 = 1 - 2x + 3x² - 4x³ and multiplying by √(1-e²) ≈ 1 - ½e² gives 1 + e² - (2e + 2e³)cosV + (3/2)e² cos2V - e³ cos3V.
- With the hourly mean motion in anomaly dU = 2'27⅚'' = 147.833'', the hourly motion is 147.833(1.0002809 - 0.0335284 cosV + 0.0004214 cos2V) ≈ 147.87'' - 4.9566'' cos V.
- Hence 142.92'' ≈ 2'23'' at apogee and (as printed) 152.86'' ≈ 2'33'' at perigee.

Purpose: tabular ingredients (solar semidiameter, solar parallax, relative hourly motion) for predicting and reducing lunar eclipses. The next page does the same for the Moon via a series for c/z.
errors: Perigee hourly motion: 147.87 + 4.9566 = 152.83'', not 152.86''. Including the neglected +0.062 cos2V term gives 152.89''. The apogee value 142.92 omits that term (it would be 142.98), so the two printed extremes are mutually inconsistent at the 0.03-0.06'' level. Rounded to 2'23'' and 2'33'' the conclusion is unaffected.
½e² = 0.00014044 is printed as 0.0001405. The logarithm of the cos2V coefficient, 9.4323278, corresponds to 0.2706; 1933·½e² = 0.2715 would give log ≈ 9.4337. Trivial.
The constant term 1933·½e² ≈ +0.27'' is silently dropped. The formula '1933'' - 32.4 cos V + 0.27 cos 2V' should strictly have 1933.27''. It is negligible, as Euler himself argues for the cos2V term.
The parallax extremes are stated as 'fere 12'' ... 13''', whereas the formula gives 12.29'' and 12.71''. This is coarse but harmless given his conclusion that the variation is negligible.

Not errors but period values: a mean solar diameter of 32'13'' (the modern mean is about 31'59'') and a solar parallax of 12.5'' (the modern value is about 8.8''). The latter is consistent with pre-1761/1769 Venus-transit estimates.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine, correct tabulation of the solar semidiameter, parallax and hourly motion as cosine series in the eccentric anomaly. There are only trivial rounding and arithmetic slips (e.g. the perigee value 152.86 should be 152.83). The only mildly interesting historical data are the adopted constants (e = 0.0167595, diameter 32'13'', parallax 12.5'', hourly anomaly 2'27⅚''), which help date the manuscript to before the Venus-transit parallax results. Nothing mathematically new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: the image reads 'Quando autem sol in hac distantia [media] a terra versatur'; the word 'media' is cut by the page edge, so the bracketed [?] can be resolved as 'media'.
Line 5: the cut-off formula is 'In distantia ergo y = a(1 + e cos V)'.
The parallax sentence reads 'erit pro quavis distantia y, quae anomaliae excentricae V convenit'; the cut word is 'quae'.
The parallax formula is printed '= 12½'' - 0,2 cos V', with 'cos V' cut at the margin.
§3 'unde si dU denotet motum horarium' — 'denotet' is partly cut at the margin.
